headline: HRV fell 12 points overnight, so both 18-minute blocks come off today - that is the gate, not my opinion.
body:
Ignore what last night's brief said about pushing; the number changed. **HRV is 48 against a 14-day mean of 61** - down 22%, and the second-lowest of the block after the 47 that followed your 16 km run. That is two mornings under baseline in a row, which drops the next session to easy. Yesterday was a 50-minute swim and light Legs. A drop that size off that load is not the session, it is you.

The swim landed as written: **2,020 m at 2:04/100 m on 131 bpm** - ten seconds per 100 m slower than 27 August and ten beats easier, which is what steady asks for. The pool is answered; Sunday's sea swim is not.

Today: **60 minutes at 131-145 bpm**, 26-28 km/h on the flat, climbs capped at 150, keep pedalling over the top. No blocks. Keep Push, stop two reps short.

Nothing else is off - RHR 45, 7.9 hours, 76 min deep. If it rebounds, Thursday's run takes the intensity. If it does not, tell me: both illnesses started exactly here.
